comment: Machine-readable table behind docs/skills/proofci. Each entry is a complete a.ts compiled by typescript/constructs.test.mjs: `supported` must translate AND emit `def a.f` in the generated Lean, `refused` must fail with a reason containing the entry's `reason` substring and the stable `code` (refusalCode from typescript/hints.mjs — the value a gaps.jsonl `code` copies). `supported` means translates, not proves — entries with `bridge` often end STUCK in the generated faithfulness proof. Keep every construct the skill claims in sync with this file; leave out anything you can't test.

supported.source: export function f(a: number, b: number): number { return a * 2 + b - 1; }

supported.construct: if / else if / else and early return
supported.source: export function f(a: number): number { if (a < 0) return 0; if (a === 0) return 1; return a; }
export function f(a: number | null): number { if (a === null) return 0; return a; }
export function f(a: number | undefined): number { return a === undefined ? 0 : a; }

supported.construct: a != null && b != null as separate nested tests
supported.source: export function f(a: number | null, b: number | null): number { if (a === null) return 0; if (b === null) return 0; return a + b; }
export function f(a: number | null, b: number): number { return (a ?? b) || 7; }
interface A { n: number } export function f(a: A | null): number { return a?.n ?? 0; }
supported.bridge: often STUCK — rewrites that worked: switch on the inductive over filter/includes/map chains; plain-field reads over ?. chains and record params

supported.source: type Role = "admin" | "member" | "guest"; export function f(r: Role): number { if (r === "admin") return 2; return 1; }
type Shape = { kind: "circle"; r: number } | { kind: "square"; side: number }; export function f(s: Shape): number { switch (s.kind) { case "circle": return s.r; case "square": return s.side; } }
interface P { x: number; y: number } export function f(p: P): number { return p.x + p.y; }
supported.bridge: often STUCK — rewrites that worked: switch on the inductive over filter/includes/map chains; plain-field reads over ?. chains and record params

supported.construct: arrays: length, indexing, map, filter, some, every, find, slice, includes, indexOf, join (strings only)
supported.source: export function f(xs: number[]): string { const ys = xs.map(x => x + 1).filter(x => x > 2); if (ys.some(x => x === 3) && xs.every(x => x >= 0)) return `${xs.map(x => `${x}`).join(",")}:${ys.slice(0, 2).length}:${ys.find(x => x > 4) ?? 0}:${xs.indexOf(1)}`; return "none"; }
supported.bridge: often STUCK — rewrites that worked: switch on the inductive over filter/includes/map chains; plain-field reads over ?. chains and record params

supported.construct: strings: length, startsWith, includes, slice, trim, split, toUpperCase
supported.source: export function f(s: string): number { const t = s.trim().toUpperCase(); if (t.startsWith("AB") && t.includes("CD")) return t.slice(1, 3).length + s.split(",").length; return t.length; }
export function f(name: string, n: number): string { return `${name}-${n}`; }

supported.construct: remainder %, Math.floor/ceil/trunc of a / b, Math.abs/min/max
supported.source: export function f(a: number, b: number): number { return (a % 4) + Math.floor(a / b) + Math.ceil(a / 2) + Math.trunc(b / 3) + Math.abs(a) + Math.min(a, b) + Math.max(a, 0); }
export function f(a: number): number { let x = a; x += 2; x++; let y: number; if (x > 0) { y = x; } else { y = 0; } return y; }
export function f(xs: number[]): number { let t = 0; for (const x of xs) { if (x < 0) continue; t += x; if (t > 100) break; } let i = 0; while (i < xs.length) { t += 1; i++; } return t; }

supported.construct: throw new Error inside a function
supported.source: export function f(a: number): number { if (a < 0) { throw new Error("neg"); } return a; }

supported.construct: in-place change to a fresh array copy, returned
supported.source: export function f(xs: number[]): number[] { const ys = [...xs]; ys.push(1); return ys; }

supported.construct: a call to a named module-level function
supported.source: function g(x: number): number { return x + 1; } export function f(x: number): number { return g(x) * 2; }

supported.construct: inline callback calling a named function
supported.source: function g(x: number): number { return x + 1; } export function f(xs: number[]): number { return xs.map(x => g(x)).length; }

supported.construct: Record<string, V>: key read, `k in r`, Object.keys
supported.source: export function f(r: Record<string, number>, k: string): number { if (k in r) { const v = r[k]; return v === undefined ? 0 : v; } return Object.keys(r).length; }
supported.bridge: often STUCK — rewrites that worked: switch on the inductive over filter/includes/map chains; plain-field reads over ?. chains and record params

supported.source: export function f(n: number): number { if (n <= 0) return 0; return 1 + f(n - 1); }

refused.workaround: drop the typeof test or test for null/undefined directly (`x == null`); the declared type already says it
refused.source: export function f(x: string | undefined): number { if (typeof x !== "string") return 0; return x.length; }

refused.construct: a != null && b != null as one condition
refused.workaround: test each value for null on its own first (`if (a === null) return ...; if (b === null) return ...`)
refused.source: export function f(a: number | null, b: number | null): number { return a != null && b != null ? a + b : 0; }

refused.workaround: write the real type
refused.source: export function f(a: any): number { return 1; }

refused.workaround: write the real type
refused.source: export function f(a: unknown): number { return 1; }

refused.workaround: split the function at the boundary: pass a `string`/`number` the pure core needs (e.g. call `.toISOString()` in a thin wrapper)
refused.source: export function f(d: Date): number { return d.getTime(); }

refused.construct: enum type (e.g. a Prisma enum import)
refused.workaround: replace the enum with a string-literal union (`type T = "a" | "b"`) and compare with the strings
refused.source: enum Color { Red, Blue } export function f(c: Color): number { return c === Color.Red ? 1 : 0; }

refused.workaround: write the parameter's type; annotate the return type too — the manifest requires written types on every function a guarantee reaches
refused.source: export function f(a): number { return a; }

refused.workaround: guard with `!== undefined` then index plainly (`v !== undefined ? v[key] : ...`)
refused.source: export function f(r: Record<string, number> | undefined, k: string): number { return r?.[k] ?? 0; }

refused.workaround: read the field and compare with `undefined` (`x.field !== undefined`) when the field is only set when defined
refused.source: interface Q { tag?: string } export function f(q: Q): number { return "tag" in q ? 1 : 0; }

refused.construct: in-place mutation of a parameter or a value another name can see
refused.workaround: change a copy (`const next = [...xs]` or `{ ...obj }`) and return it
refused.source: export function f(xs: number[]): number[] { xs.push(1); return xs; }

refused.construct: a literal-union member that is not a Lean name (`"NOT IN"`)
refused.workaround: rename the member to a Lean-safe ASCII name (letters, digits, `_`)
refused.source: type Op = "IN" | "NOT IN"; export function f(o: Op): number { return o === "IN" ? 1 : 0; }

refused.workaround: pass the plain fields the function needs in an interface instead of the instance
refused.source: class Db { get(): number { return 1; } } export function f(db: Db): number { return db.get(); }

refused.workaround: take an array parameter instead
refused.source: export function f(...xs: number[]): number { return xs.length; }

refused.workaround: use an interface with named fields
refused.source: export function f(p: [number, number]): number { return p[0]; }

refused.workaround: keep only plain fields in the interface
refused.source: interface A { x: number; g(): void } export function f(a: A): number { return a.x; }

refused.workaround: parse at the boundary and pass typed values in; `JSON` has no model
refused.source: export function f(s: string): number { return JSON.parse(s).length; }
refused.reason: isn't to a function the translator can see

refused.workaround: remove the logging from the function a guarantee reaches
refused.source: export function f(a: number): number { console.log(a); return a; }
refused.reason: isn't to a function the translator can see

refused.workaround: inline literal arithmetic (e.g. `quota * 8 / 10` for `Math.ceil(quota * 0.8)`)
refused.source: export function f(a: number): number { return Math.pow(a, 2); }

refused.construct: index into a `Record<string, V>` module constant (const-map lookup)
refused.workaround: inline the literal where it is read, or replace the lookup with a `switch` that returns per-case literals
refused.source: const M: Record<string, number> = { a: 1, b: 2 }; export function f(k: string): number { return M[k] ?? 0; }

refused.construct: `NoInfer<T>` and other inference-marker / schema-derived types (`z.infer` aliases)
refused.workaround: write the resolved type out by hand
refused.source: export function f<T>(x: T, y: NoInfer<T>): number { return 1; }
